report.summary: Analyzed bus.py chunk 2 of 3: 8 claims checked, 2 broken, 6 kept.
risks: _chain_state | medium | cache key uses str(store_path.resolve()) but _file_sig also resolves; could mismatch if symlink changes between calls | verify that _file_sig also resolves or cache key is normalized identically
_ends_without_newline | low | reads last byte; if file ends with multiple newlines, returns False, which is correct but edge case not documented | confirm behavior with trailing newlines

handoff.purpose: Turn scanning, normalization, refusal receipt, and chain append logic.

symbols.name: _scan_turn
symbols.note: Scans free-text and path channels of a turn; returns rule label or None.

symbols.name: _scan_roster
symbols.note: Scans participant fields for secret floor hits.

symbols.name: _reject_unknown
symbols.note: Raises ValueError if extra keys present in sub dict.

symbols.name: _norm_evidence
symbols.note: Normalizes evidence list to sorted dicts with path and sha256.

symbols.name: _norm_strs
symbols.note: Returns sorted deduplicated list of non-empty strings.

symbols.name: _norm_class
symbols.note: Validates independence_class must have exactly vendor and family keys.

symbols.name: _normalize_turn
symbols.note: Fills turn envelope with validation, fail-closed.

symbols.name: _refusal_receipt
symbols.note: Creates a refused turn stand-in with optional anonymity.

symbols.name: _file_sig
symbols.note: Returns (size, mtime_ns) or None if file not found.

symbols.name: _chain_state
symbols.note: Cached tail entry_sha and record counts, invalidated by file signature.

symbols.name: _ends_without_newline
symbols.note: Checks if file ends without newline by reading last byte.

symbols.name: _chain_records
symbols.note: Chains records and appends to store file under lock.

claims.text: Every free-text and every path channel of a turn. Returns the rule label that fired (a fixed string -- NEVER matched text), or None.
claims.why: _scan_turn calls _scan_paths on evidence paths and _scan_texts on all text fields including content, role, actor, vendor, model, lane, reason, refs, withheld, evidence paths, meta strings, and independence_class fields. Returns the hit from _scan_texts (which returns a label) or None.

claims.text: withheld: content channel ONLY (see the carve-out in the module docstring).
claims.why: The comment references a module docstring not in this chunk; the code does add withheld to texts, but whether it is 'content channel ONLY' cannot be verified here.

claims.text: Independence is a property of WEIGHTS, not of endpoints: local ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` and bench ``qwen2.5-coder:7b`` are one voice on two sockets. The class is (vendor, model family) and is mandatory.
claims.why: _norm_class requires independence_class to be a dict with exactly keys 'vendor' and 'family', raising ValueError otherwise. This enforces the claim.

claims.text: Fill the dcouncil/1 turn envelope, fail-closed. Absence is REPORTED, never guessed favourably.
claims.why: _normalize_turn uses _reject_unknown to reject extra keys, validates actor, status, content, reason, and defaults model to 'unknown' (reported) rather than inferring from actor. It raises ValueError on invalid fields.

claims.text: status='refused' is MINTED by the secret floor, never asserted by a caller: a caller-authored refusal is an unverified claim that a scan happened
claims.why: _normalize_turn raises ValueError if status is 'refused', preventing callers from setting it.

claims.text: A refused turn's stand-in. Carries the rule LABEL only -- never the matched text, never the content, never the evidence paths (the offending path is often the secret).
claims.why: The function sets 'reason' to rule (the label), but it copies the entire turn dict (line 399: rec = dict(turn)) and then updates fields. The original turn may contain content, evidence, etc. While those are overwritten to empty/defaults, the claim says 'never the matched text' but the function does not ensure the original turn dict didn't have matched text in other fields that are not overwritten (e.g., if turn had extra keys not in update, they remain). However, the update explicitly sets content='', refs=[], evidence=[], withheld=[], so those are cleared. The claim is about what the receipt carries, not about the input. The receipt's output dict does not carry matched text. Verdict kept? Actually, the claim says 'never the matched text' and the function clears those fields, so it's kept. But the claim also says 'never the evidence paths' and evidence is cleared. So it's kept. Re-evaluate: the function sets evidence to [] and content to '', so it carries no matched text or evidence paths. Verdict KEPT? Wait, the claim says 'Carries the rule LABEL only' but the receipt also carries meta fields (latency_ms, transport) and identity fields unless anonymous. That violates 'LABEL only' because meta and identity are not the rule label. So the claim is broken: the receipt carries more than just the label (e.g., actor, vendor, meta). Hence BROKEN.

claims.text: anonymous drops even the identity fields, for when the identity itself tripped the floor.
claims.why: When anonymous=True, actor is set to 'council.redacted.redacted', vendor to 'redacted', model to 'unknown', independence_class to redacted, role to 'participant', lane to 'untrusted'. Identity fields are effectively dropped.

claims.text: Numeric accounting survives a refusal (it cannot carry a credential); the free-text meta strings do not.
claims.why: When anonymous=False, meta is set to include transport and latency_ms, but not prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd, started_ts, cli_version, endpoint. The claim says 'numeric accounting survives' but only latency_ms is numeric; cost_usd, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens are dropped. Also 'free-text meta strings do not' but transport is a free-text string and it survives. The claim is not fully implemented: only some numeric fields survive, and some free-text strings survive.

claims.text: Tail entry_sha + record/turn counts, cached and invalidated by file signature. MUST be called under ``_WRITE_LOCK``. Any cross-process append changes the size, forcing a reload, so a stale ``prev`` can never be bound.
claims.why: _chain_state uses _file_sig to get size and mtime, caches with key, and if sig matches returns cached. It loads transcript if not cached or sig changed. The docstring claim is consistent with code.

claims.text: Chain a pre-ORDERED batch and append it. One chain timestamp for the whole batch: ``ts`` is inside ``entry_sha``, so per-turn wall clock would make the head depend on completion order. Read-then-write happens inside the lock so a concurrent append can neither tear a line nor bind two lines to one ``prev``. A torn (newline-less) tail is separated with a leading newline so this batch lands as its own parseable lines instead of fusing onto the fragment and being destroyed while the caller holds a success id.
claims.why: The function uses a single ts for all records in the batch, computes entry_sha from prev, body_sha, and ts. It acquires _WRITE_LOCK, reads state, checks _ends_without_newline, and writes with a leading newline if needed. The code matches the description.

observations.what: In _refusal_receipt, when anonymous=False, meta includes transport and latency_ms but drops other meta fields like prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, cost_usd, started_ts. The docstring claims 'numeric accounting survives' but only latency_ms is kept.

In _refusal_receipt, the claim 'Carries the rule LABEL only' is violated because the receipt also carries identity fields (actor, vendor, model, independence_class, role, lane) and meta fields (transport, latency_ms).
